what: Release 1 train R1g: every suite id that tools/t0/run_suites.mjs defines for the command below, with its last known result and the log that result is read from. A suite with no row in any log is marked never_reached. This file records; it does not judge: no row is classified here.
generated_by: node tools/t0/r1g/suites_status.mjs (inputs: the runner's --list and the logs of tools/t0/r1g/suites_sources.json; regenerate after every new run, check with --check)
how_to_read: last = the row of the newest run (by time_utc of its source entry) that has a row for the suite; earlier = its rows in older runs, newest first. status, result, seconds, tiles and load are copied from the log line (log_line is its line number in the archived log; log_original is where the log was written).
ok true means the runner printed PASS (for a green row: every selected test passed, skips are counted separately; for a check row: the expected exit code).

failing_tests_printed are the test ids on the indented FAIL lines under the row and failing_lines_printed those lines as the runner printed them (last only); the runner prints at most 8 per suite and 6 per parallel slice, so failing_tests_truncated marks a longer list. summary_tail (last only, rows that are not ok) is the last output lines the runner stored in the summary JSON of the same run.

seconds are the wall-clock time of the suite as the runner printed it. Every log was written on the cloud machine (4 vCPU container, software GL), so no duration is comparable with the Windows acceptance machine. load1Start / load1End are the machine's 1-minute load average at the start and end of the suite; null in every log written before the runner recorded it (2026-11-13). A timing failure measured at a load above 3 is not evidence and is re-run later.
newer_runs_that_stopped_before_it names the stopped runs, newer than the last result, that had selected the suite and ended before reaching it: the last result is then older than the latest attempt.

The logs and summaries are byte-identical copies (cmp, 2026-11-13) of files written under tmp/ (git-ignored); sources[].conditions says under which conditions each run was made and which record says so. A result is the state of the tree and of the runner of its own run, not of today.

To run one suite alone: the command with --only <id>. --only matches by prefix (static.legal also selects static.legal.optin, r1.polish also r1.polish.pair, a11y.R1c also a11y.R1c.tiles, pagescore.R1c also pagescore.R1c.real and .full).

sources.conditions: Cloud container, 2026-11-13, a verification run of the final proxy-aware runner (one suite, which downloads the pinned Mapbox GL library with its own Node fetch() code (tests/t0/pages-maps.spec.mjs)): `node tools/t0/run_suites.mjs --r1-dist release/R1g/dist --no-red --no-network --only pagesmaps.R1a --port-base 19040` (1 rows: pagesmaps.R1a; a prefix in --only can select more than one suite), started by the run script tmp/r1g-verify2/e2e-inner.sh inside one slot of the machine lock, with no manual environment: by its header the shell had HTTPS_PROXY set and NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY unset (its summary says the children's environment got: added NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY; extended NODE_OPTIONS). Header written by the run script: maps start 2026-11-14T00:04:03Z load1 13.24; HTTPS_PROXY set: yes; NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=<unset>; NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt; NODE_OPTIONS=--use-openssl-ca; T0_MAPBOX_UNREACHABLE=<unset>; vendor caches before: ls: cannot access 'tmp/r1g-verify2-maps/vendor': No such file or directory ls: cannot access 'tmp/t0-maps/vendor': No such file or directory  / maps end 2026-11-14T00:04:06Z load1 13.62; runner exit 1; vendor cache after: mapbox-gl.css mapbox-gl.js. Runner exit code 1. Rows: pagesmaps.R1a FAIL 1/1. Load recorded: 13.24 at the start and 13.62 at the end of the run, 4 CPUs, shared with other work: the durations are not timing evidence (measured on the cloud machine (4 vCPU container, software GL)). The run reached its final line. This entry was written by tmp/r1g-verify2/register.mjs from the summary JSON, the header file, the exit-code file and the run script; it made no diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS ADDED 2026-11-14 by the release-r1g engineer (a diagnosis, not a fact that run recorded: its header does not list T0_CHROME). The summary tail of the row (three lines: '  ]', '}', 'Node.js v22.23.4') and the row itself (1 PASS line, then the process ended with exit 1 after 2.5 s) are what an unhandled Node error that ends a suite after its first test looks like. The vendor cache after the run held mapbox-gl.css and mapbox-gl.js, so the download through the proxy that the runner enables had worked. Reproduced the same day on the same tree, without a browser starting: with the harness environment added by hand (NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1, NODE_OPTIONS='--use-openssl-ca --disable-warning=UNDICI-EHPA', as child_env.mjs gives it), a cold vendor cache and T0_CHROME UNSET, `node tests/t0/pages-maps.spec.mjs --dist release/R1g/dist --filter 'PG-01|PG-02-camera'` printed PG-01 PASS and then died with 'Error: spawn C:/Program Files/Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe ENOENT' (tests/t0/lib.mjs: CHROME = T0_CHROME or the Windows path; the spawn has no 'error' handler), its last three lines being '  ]', '}', 'Node.js v22.23.4', exit 1, 6.5 s wall (log docs/accept/r1g-suite-logs/2026-11-14-pagesmaps-no-chrome-repro.log). Control, same suite in the shell as the container gives it (HTTPS_PROXY set, NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY unset, T0_CHROME set, cold cache): PG-02-camera FAIL 'TypeError: fetch failed' in ensureVendor and no vendor file written (log docs/accept/r1g-suite-logs/2026-11-14-pagesmaps-no-proxy-env-control.log), which is the failure that the summary tails of the pagesfix rows of the full run of 2026-11-11 show ('TypeError: fetch failed' in ensureVendor; the tails of the pagesmaps rows of that run do not name the cause, but the 20 tests that failed in them are the ones that call ensureVendor) and what the proxy rule removes. The repeat of this run with T0_CHROME set was queued behind the machine lock when this diagnosis was written (tmp/r1g-final/e2e-inner.sh); when it has run, its entry is the one whose log is docs/accept/r1g-suite-logs/2026-11-14-pagesmaps-cold-cache-chrome-set.log.
